---
title: Run it yourself
description: Postgres in Docker, a free NEAR testnet account as your operator, a free Privy app, and two commands.
icon: Terminal
---

You need Node 22.18 or newer, pnpm 11, Docker, and a free [Privy](https://dashboard.privy.io) app with email login.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install and configure

```bash
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env          # fill in POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DATABASE_URL and the four PRIVY_ values
pnpm services:up              # Postgres on 127.0.0.1:54330
pnpm db:migrate
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Make your operator

```bash
node scripts/testnet-account.mjs my-studio.testnet   # a free testnet account
```

Set `NETWORKS.testnet.operator` in `packages/config/src/index.ts` to that account. It becomes the parent of every
user account (`name.my-studio.testnet`). Then:

```bash
pnpm ops add-keys testnet 3   # writes OPERATOR_KEYS_TESTNET to .env
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Run

```bash
pnpm dev                      # the web app on :3100, the worker, and these docs on :3300
```

</Step>
</Steps>

For **Add test dollars**, send your operator some test USDC from [Circle's faucet](https://faucet.circle.com).
`pnpm ci` runs Biome, the type checks, the tests and the build.

## Environment

| Name | For |
| --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Postgres |
| `APP_URL` | The web app's public address |
| `PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_VERIFICATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Email sign-in |
| `OPERATOR_KEYS_TESTNET` | The worker only: the operator's keys |
| `OPERATOR_KEYS_MAINNET` | The worker only: `tegata.near`'s keys. They turn Live on in the worker |
| `LIVE_ENABLED` | `true` tells the web server Live is on, without giving it the mainnet keys |
| `SESSION_SECRET` | Signs the session cookie of people who sign in with a NEAR wallet (32 characters or more) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM` | Every email; leave both empty and Tegata issues links only |
| `ONECLICK_API_KEY` | Optional 1Click partner key; without it 1Click adds its own small fee |
| `NOAH_API_KEY`, `SOLANA_DEVNET_ADDRESS`, `SOLANA_DEVNET_SECRET` | [Bank](/docs/guide/bank) on Noah's sandbox; the Solana secret is the worker's only |
| `BITNOB_CLIENT_ID`, `BITNOB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `BITNOB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | [Spend cards](/docs/guide/cards) |
| `TRANSAK_API_KEY`, `TRANSAK_API_SECRET`, `TRANSAK_ENV` | [Pay by card](/docs/guide/cards#customers-who-pay-by-card): staging keys in the Sandbox, production keys in Live |

`ALLOW_LOCAL_WEBHOOKS=true` lets a development server send webhooks to `http://localhost`; production always
requires public https.

Every partner is optional: without its keys, that part of the app says so and the rest works.
